target.title: Add configurable descriptive agent session labels
target.body:
## Summary

- add an Agent sessions label setting with Project, Descriptive, and Descriptive + project modes
- use Codex thread titles for main sessions, named task paths for subagents, and a clear Approval review label for guardians
- keep Project as the compatibility default and fall back to the project whenever descriptive metadata is unavailable
- carry the optional descriptive name through remote session JSON without breaking older payloads

## Why

Agent session rows currently use only the working-directory basename. When several Codex sessions share one repository, every row can have the same label even though Codex already stores useful chat titles and subagent task names.

This makes the behavior configurable instead of replacing the existing label style for everyone.

## Implementation notes

- reads only the requested Codex thread rows from the newest `state_*.sqlite` database
- gracefully falls back when the database or newer columns are unavailable
- removes command preambles and caps long automatic titles at 64 characters
- continues using project names for Claude Code because equivalent title metadata is not currently exposed

## Validation

- `swift build --target CodexBarCore` passed with the compatible installed SDK
- `swift build --target CodexBarCLI` passed from current head `2370d11d57b7cfa2d95e4d95cd59c08c0af57689`
- `CodexBarCLI sessions --json` passed against live local session metadata and produced compact descriptive names
- SwiftFormat lint passed for all Sources and Tests
- app locale, documentation, packaging, signing-path, sharding, CI-path, repository-size, shell, and site checks passed
- full Swift tests and SwiftLint could not run locally because this Mac's Command Line Tools compiler, SDK, Testing framework, and SourceKit installation are mismatched; macOS CI is required before review completion

### Redacted runtime proof

Captured from current head on July 17, 2026. The first scan used the live Codex home and resolved the thread title:

```json
[
  {
    "provider": "codex",
    "source": "ide",
    "state": "active",
    "projectName": "<redacted project>",
    "sessionName": "Fix Claude reauthorization"
  }
]
```

For the missing-metadata case, the same live rollout was copied into an isolated `CODEX_HOME` with no `state_*.sqlite` database. The CLI kept the project name and returned no descriptive name:

```json
[
  {
    "provider": "codex",
    "source": "ide",
    "state": "active",
    "projectName": "<redacted project>",
    "sessionName": null
  }
]
```

That second result exercises the menu fallback: Descriptive and Descriptive + project use `projectName` when `sessionName` is absent. Project remains the persisted default.

target.title: feat: add codexbar cookie refresh CLI command
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `codexbar cookie refresh --provider <name>` CLI command to force re-import of browser cookies for cookie-authenticated providers.

**Note:** Settings-pane refresh buttons (↻) split into a separate PR: **#2264**.

## Behaviour

- `codexbar cookie refresh --provider opencodego` — clears Keychain cache, re-imports from all supported browsers, stores fresh cookie
- `codexbar cookie refresh --all` — refreshes OpenCode and OpenCode Go
- Falls back gracefully when `importSession` fails (code-signing entitlements required)
- Supports `--format text|json`, `--json`, `--json-only`, `--pretty`
- Uses the provider's automatic browser import order (scans all installed browsers via `preferredBrowsers: []`)

## Verified Behaviour

### Evidence

See `docs/proof/cli-cookie-refresh-proof.md` for full test matrix.

Key results:

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `cookie refresh --provider opencodego` | ✅ JSON output: `"status": "cleared"` |
| Before: Keychain `cookie.opencodego` | `storedAt: 2026-07-17T18:25:50Z` |
| After: Keychain lookup | ❌ Not found (cache cleared) |
| After CodexBar.app refresh | ✅ Cookie re-imported with fresh `storedAt` |
| `--provider nonexistent` | ✅ `"Unknown provider: nonexistent"` |
| `--all` | ✅ Targets only OpenCode + OpenCodeGo |
| `--format json --pretty` | ✅ Valid JSON output |
| Build | ✅ `swift build` zero errors |

### End-to-end flow

```
CLI command                         CodexBar.app (menu bar)
┌──────────────────────┐            ┌─────────────────────┐
│ cookie refresh       │            │ auto-refresh detects │
│ --provider opencodego│            │ missing cache        │
│                      │            │                      │
│ ① Clear Keychain ✅  │  ──────→  │ ② SweetCookieKit     │
│ ② Import browser ❌  │  (fail)   │    import from Chrome │
│    (unsigned binary) │            │ ③ Store in Keychain  │
│ ③ Print "cleared"    │            │ ④ Refresh usage ✅   │
└──────────────────────┘            └─────────────────────┘
```

### Known Limitation

`OpenCodeCookieImporter.importSession()` requires code-signing entitlements unavailable in debug CLI builds. The command clears the cache and falls back — the actual re-import happens when CodexBar.app (with proper entitlements) refreshes. Same behaviour as `codexbar cache clear --cookies` which also clears without importing.

## Related

- Issue: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2260
- Settings PR: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2264

## Summary

- estimate remaining weekly quota as full 5-hour windows from the median burn across the latest seven completed active session windows
- show the estimate verdict first, then the numeric headroom line, only after at least three reliable samples
- support Codex, Claude, Antigravity/Gemini, and generic providers with unambiguous session/weekly pairs
- respect weekly work-day settings, isolate provider/account/window history, and memoize the existing history scan
- localize the new pluralized output and accessibility labels across all 23 catalogs

Addresses #2261. The issue remains open for reporter confirmation.

## Verification

- `swift test --filter SessionEquivalentForecastTests` — 23 tests passed
- `swift test --filter 'SessionEquivalentForecastTests|UsageStorePlanUtilizationTests'` — 101 tests passed
- source-blind behavior contract — 19 feature cases passed
- `make check` — SwiftFormat, SwiftLint, localization, docs, scripts, and repository gates passed
- all 23 stringsdict catalogs passed `plutil -lint`
- full sharded suite on the feature head before the final isolation hardening — 700 selections passed; exact-head CI is the final full-suite gate
- repeated branch autoreview; all accepted findings fixed, including named-window isolation and preservation of generic weekly reset/history behavior

## Presentation

Verdict leads; numeric estimate follows. The reporter has not answered the ordering question yet, so this uses the owner-approved default.

## Summary

Related to #384.

## Redacted runtime proof

I ran the branch against an actual OMP session. The first command reads only metadata and redacts the session filename and token counts:

```console
$ jq '<select first OMP openai-codex assistant message and redact usage>' ~/.omp/agent/sessions/<redacted>.jsonl
{"source":"~/.omp/agent/sessions/<redacted>.jsonl","provider":"openai-codex","api":"openai-codex-responses","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","usage":{"input":"<redacted>","cacheRead":"<redacted>","output":"<redacted>","totalTokens":"<redacted>"}}
```

A fresh local Codex cost scan on the same branch reports that OMP model. Token and cost values are redacted:

```console
$ CodexBarCLI cost --provider codex --format json --refresh --days 1 | jq '<retain source/model and redact usage>'
[
  {
    "provider": "codex",
    "source": "local",
    "daily": [
      {
        "date": "2026-07-17",
        "modelsUsed": ["gpt-5.6-sol"],
        "inputTokens": "<redacted>",
        "cacheReadTokens": "<redacted>",
        "outputTokens": "<redacted>",
        "totalTokens": "<redacted>",
        "totalCost": "<redacted>"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

## Verification
- `swift test --build-system native --filter 'scanner merges omp sessions with pi sessions'`
